rows.n: F1 score
rows.b: A balance of precision and recall into one number, common for question-answering tests.

rows.n: feed-forward network
rows.b: The per-position mini-network inside each transformer block that transforms the attention output into richer features.

rows.n: fertility
rows.b: How many tokens a tokenizer produces per word on average — lower means cheaper, faster processing.

rows.n: few-shot evaluation
rows.b: Testing with a few examples in the prompt, the standard fair-comparison setup.

rows.n: few-shot prompting
rows.b: Showing the model a few examples inside the prompt so it copies the pattern.

rows.n: fine-tuning
rows.b: Extra training on a smaller, focused dataset to teach a pretrained model a particular skill, tone, or task.

rows.n: forward pass
rows.b: Running input through the model to produce predictions, the first half of every training step.

rows.n: FP16
rows.b: 16-bit floating point numbers — half the memory of FP32, standard for fast training.

rows.n: frequency penalty
rows.b: A penalty that grows the more a token repeats, taming loops without banning words outright.

rows.n: FSDP
rows.b: Fully sharded data parallel: spreading the model's parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across GPUs to train giants.

rows.n: function calling
rows.b: Letting the model request real actions, like checking weather, by emitting structured calls a program executes.
